subject: Civil Engineering
title: Soil Compaction and Preloading
description: One-minute skill: Soil Compaction and Preloading.

hook.text: Singapore's Changi Airport was built on reclaimed land. The soil needed years of squeezing.

buildup.text: Preloading places heavy fill on weak soil — the weight squeezes water out over months.

discovery.text: Vertical drains speed the process by giving trapped water a shortcut to escape.

twist.text: Without preloading, the airport runway would have settled unevenly for decades.

climax.text: The fill is removed after consolidation — the soil is now dense and stable forever.

punchline.text: Squeeze the water out first, then build for keeps.

quiz.question: How does preloading improve weak soil?
options: It heats the soil to bake it into a harder material
Heavy fill compresses the soil and squeezes out water, increasing density
It replaces the weak soil with stronger material from elsewhere

details.summary: Preloading improves soft compressible soil by placing surcharge fill weight on the site to force consolidation settlement before construction begins. Vertical drains called wick drains are installed to speed drainage from clay layers that would otherwise take years to consolidate.
details.whyItMatters: Preloading converts unacceptably soft ground into buildable land at lower cost than deep foundations or soil replacement. Combining preloading with wick drains makes it practical for time-sensitive projects.
takeaways: Surcharge fill loads force water out of compressible clay, strengthening it over time
Wick drains shorten drainage paths from meters to tens of centimeters
Preloading is removed after target settlement is achieved, leaving improved ground

faq.question: How do wick drains accelerate consolidation of soft clay?
faq.answer: Wick drains are thin, corrugated plastic strips that provide drainage channels vertically through the clay layer. Without drains, water must travel horizontally to natural drainage boundaries, which may be meters away.

faq.question: How is the progress of preloading monitored?
faq.answer: Settlement plates on the ground surface measure total settlement over time. Piezometers installed in the clay layer monitor pore pressure dissipation. When pore pressures have dissipated to the target level and settlement rate has slowed sufficiently.
